current.text: He is expected to start at center. Milwaukee's projected starters are Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Turner.
Milwaukee traded for Kel'el Ware, another center. Power forward is the team's weakest position, so the team will likely start a center at the four.
Ware may limit his minutes, and his outlook would be better without Ware on the roster. Other experts think Turner and Ware can play together and that Turner is still the better player.
Doc Rivers, who often benched him for Jericho Sims, is no longer the coach. Taylor Jenkins is the new coach.
He is a strong bounce-back candidate and should not be written off. His minutes should rise to about 29, with 14 points, 6 rebounds, 2 threes and 2 blocks a reasonable target and top-60 upside.
Experts call him fair value around pick 120 to 128 and too expensive near picks 86 to 100. In an auction mock Josh valued him at 1 to 3 USD, and he went for 6 USD.
Milwaukee is expected to be a bad team but does not own its draft pick, so it has no reason to tank.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category, clearly above the top 250 pool.
He makes about 2 threes per game, many for a center.
His FG% is weak for a center, so he fits a punt FG% build.
He needs good point guard play in the pick and roll. When he is mostly parked in the corner, he is not used well.
He is worth less in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Turner is a cheap block and three-point center for us. Yahoo values him at 5 USD and ESPN at 3 USD, and a recent mock priced him at 1 to 6 USD, so the 20 USD our league paid last season is far too much. He fits punt FG% builds best, because his projected 45.8% FG% is weak for a center while his 1.7 blocks and 2 threes are strong. Early in the season, check whether Taylor Jenkins gives him about 29 minutes next to Kel'el Ware, and whether his usage climbs back above last season's 18%.
